mstts:express-as.prosody: Imagine a world where, even in the midst of all the noise and uncertainty, the quiet strength of virtue is what truly shapes our lives. When everything around us seems to be changing at lightning speed, it’s those timeless qualities—honesty, integrity, compassion—that keep us grounded, and help us build families and communities that last. Now, what if we could rediscover those values and bring them back to the center of our lives? That’s exactly the journey we’re about to take together, inspired by Gordon B. Hinckley’s heartfelt wisdom in his book, Standing for Something: 10 Neglected Virtues That Will Heal Our Hearts and Homes. As we explore, we’ll shine a light on ten remarkable virtues—each one offering a powerful way to nurture relationships, strengthen families, and bring a sense of hope back into our world. Through stories and gentle insights, we’ll see just how much these virtues can transform not only our own hearts, but also the homes and communities we’re part of. So, let’s walk this path together—open to reflection, ready to grow, and committed to making a difference, starting from within. With every step, you’ll discover new possibilities for healing, purpose, and a life that feels a little more meaningful each day. Here’s to a journey filled with kindness, courage, and moral clarity—one virtue at a time.

Chapter One: Rediscovering the Power of Virtue in Everyday Life
Have you ever felt like something fundamental is missing from our daily lives? With the constant buzz of screens and every hour packed to the brim, it’s easy to think the quiet strength of old-fashioned virtues is just a memory from some distant past. But deep down, so many of us still crave decency, kindness, and a real sense of purpose—a way to anchor ourselves and our families when the world feels a little unsteady.
The real story doesn’t begin with anything grand. It actually starts in those small, everyday moments. Maybe it’s a neighbor who waves from across the street, then stops to help you with your groceries. Or a child, worn out from the day, curling up next to their parent for comfort. It’s in these ordinary, almost unnoticed exchanges that the seeds of something far greater are quietly planted. This journey is about learning to notice those moments—to see them as the real foundation for a life built on virtue.
It feels like society’s drifted—not because anyone’s truly bad, but because we’ve let go of the habits that used to hold us together. The virtues that shaped entire generations—like honesty, respect, and gratitude—often get lost in the shuffle, overshadowed by cynicism or the chase for quick rewards. And it leaves a lot of us wondering: Whatever happened to the values that made families strong and neighborhoods safe? Why do we sometimes feel alone, even when we’re surrounded by people?
The answer isn’t found in new gadgets or sweeping changes. It’s hidden in the simple, quiet choice to stand for something. To pick integrity over what’s easy, and to nurture the qualities that heal both hearts and homes. Here’s the inspiring part: anyone—no matter where they come from or what they’ve been through—can make a difference just by living these virtues. When one person is kind or one family makes a commitment, the ripple effect can reach much farther than you’d ever imagine.
Maybe you remember a parent, exhausted after work, who still makes time to listen to their child’s worries. The conversation isn’t long, maybe just a few words over dinner, but the impact? It’s huge. The child feels seen, valued, and safe. In that moment, the parent isn’t just providing a meal—they’re passing down a legacy of love and attention. That’s how virtue gets handed down—not through big speeches, but through quietly living it out, day after day.
Of course, living with virtue isn’t always easy. Sometimes, it’s tempting to look the other way, let a small lie slide, or ignore someone who needs help. But those are the exact moments when our character is shaped. The real call here isn’t about being perfect, but about sticking with it—choosing to keep trying, even when it’s tough or unpopular.
As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that bringing virtue back isn’t just a solo mission. It’s something we do together. Families, friends, and neighbors all have a role to play, supporting each other along the way. And the home? It’s the main workshop for building character. Kids soak up lessons not just from what we say, but from what we do every single day. When parents show honesty, forgiveness, and gratitude, those traits become part of the family’s DNA.
So, the opening chapter really sets the stage for a journey of rediscovery. It encourages us to look past the latest headlines and fleeting trends, and focus on those timeless values that have always brought people together. And here’s the hopeful message: by reclaiming these neglected virtues, each of us has the power to heal our hearts, our homes, and our communities—one small moment at a time.

Let’s explore Chapter 2: The Foundation of Love and Compassion.
At the very heart of every strong family, and every close-knit community, there’s something simple but truly powerful—love. Not just the kind you see in movies or hear about in love songs, but that steady, quiet care that shapes lives in ways you might not even notice at first.
This kind of love is the starting point for everything else. It’s like the soil where kindness, patience, and understanding can really take root and grow.
Imagine a teacher who notices a student struggling—not just with homework, but with loneliness. Instead of ignoring the quiet or brushing it off, the teacher offers a kind word and takes the time to really listen. Over time, that student’s confidence starts to blossom. And it’s not because of any big dramatic gesture—it’s simply because someone cared enough to notice. That’s love in action: seeing what someone needs, and responding with genuine concern.
In families, love often shows up in the smallest sacrifices. Picture a parent getting up early to make breakfast, even when they’re exhausted and would love just a few more minutes of sleep. Or siblings sharing their favorite toys—even if it’s not always with a smile—learning what it means to put someone else’s happiness before their own. These little moments, even when they go unnoticed, are truly the building blocks of a compassionate home.
But, let’s be honest—love isn’t always easy. There are days when tempers flare, or misunderstandings create distance. On those days, choosing to love isn’t automatic; it’s a conscious decision. It means forgiving mistakes, letting go of old grudges, and choosing to see the best in each other—even when it’s tough. And here’s something interesting: the more you practice this kind of love, the easier it becomes to extend it beyond just your family—to friends, neighbors, and even strangers.
Now, compassion is closely tied to love. It’s about truly feeling what someone else is going through, and being moved enough to help. It’s the reason you might visit a friend who’s sick, or offer to help a neighbor in need, or simply say something kind when you notice someone seems down. Compassion doesn’t require a lot of money or special skills. All it really asks for is an open heart.
Maybe you’ve seen this play out in your own life—a community coming together when a family faces tough times. People deliver meals, help out with chores, watch the kids so the parents can get a break. The family feels overwhelmed by gratitude, but also finds new strength to keep going. In those moments, you really see what compassion can do—it binds people together and creates a deep sense of belonging.
What stands out most is this: love and compassion aren’t just feelings—they’re choices you make every day. They take effort, patience, and sometimes, a willingness to be a little vulnerable. But the rewards? They’re huge. Homes filled with love become safe places where people can truly grow. Communities marked by compassion become places where everyone has a real shot at thriving.
So, as we wrap up this section, here’s the key takeaway: love is the very foundation for everything else. Without it, all the best intentions to build character or fix relationships can fall flat. But with love at the center, even the toughest challenges can be faced with hope—and a whole lot of resilience.

Chapter 3: Honesty and Integrity — The Cornerstones of Trust
Trust really is like an invisible thread, weaving its way through our relationships, our families, and even our societies. Without it, even the strongest bonds can start to come apart. But what creates that sense of trust? At the heart of it all, there’s honesty—a real commitment to being truthful, both in what we say and what we do. And right alongside honesty is integrity. That’s the quiet resolve to do the right thing, even when nobody’s watching.
I think about a story I once heard—a young employee faced with a big temptation: cut corners at work, or stick to the rules? The pressure from deadlines, the urge to make a good impression on the boss—it’s all there. After a moment’s hesitation, the employee decides to play it straight, even if it means staying late. And you know what? The relief that comes isn’t just about dodging trouble—it’s that deep, quiet satisfaction of knowing your actions match your values.
Honesty gets tested at home too, often in the smallest ways. Imagine a child who accidentally breaks a vase. Hiding what happened seems so easy. But when a parent senses something’s up and gently asks, the truth comes out. Instead of anger, there’s appreciation for the child’s courage. Over time, these moments send a clear message: honesty might not always be easy, but it’s always worth it.
Integrity isn’t just about telling the truth, though. It’s about consistency. Are you the same person in private as you are in public? Do you keep your promises and stand up for what’s right, even when it’s not the popular thing to do? Most of us find that integrity is built one decision at a time—each honest choice reinforcing the next.
I’m reminded of a community leader who once faced a tough call. Instead of taking the easy way out, this leader chose to be transparent, even though not everyone agreed with the decision. It wasn’t the popular move, but it earned real respect. People might disagree, but at least they know where their leader stands. That kind of integrity inspires others to step up with the same kind of courage.
Let’s be honest—honesty and integrity are constantly under threat these days. The world often rewards shortcuts and cleverness more than character. It’s all too easy to justify a little white lie or bend the rules when it seems like no big deal. But over time, those choices chip away at trust, making it tougher to build the relationships that matter most.
So, how do we bring honesty and integrity back to the center of our lives? It really starts at home. When parents model truthfulness, kids learn that honesty isn’t up for debate. When friends hold each other accountable, trust grows deeper. And in our workplaces and communities, leaders who act with integrity set the tone for everyone else.
Here’s the key takeaway: honesty and integrity aren’t just personal virtues—they’re public goods. When we all commit to these values, the benefits ripple outward, strengthening our families, our workplaces, and our communities. Once trust is established, it becomes the solid foundation for every other relationship in our lives.

Chapter 4: The Healing Power of Forgiveness and Gratitude.
Life’s never short on disappointments, is it? Even among the people we love most, there are moments when tempers flare and words come out that we wish we could take back. It’s in these moments—when mistakes have been made and feelings are hurt—that forgiveness becomes truly essential. Not just for the person who messed up, but for the one who’s been wounded, too.
Think about a time when a simple argument with a sibling or close friend spiraled out of control—maybe the silent treatment lasted days. Then, out of the blue, one person decides to break the ice with a quiet apology. There’s that split-second pause... and then, acceptance. Suddenly, the tension lifts, almost like a heavy weight’s been set down. In that moment, you realize—real forgiveness isn’t about pretending nothing happened, or making excuses. It’s about choosing to let go of resentment so you can both move forward.
Sometimes, people think forgiveness means weakness. But honestly? It takes real strength. It means you’re willing to face your pain, but you refuse to let it shape your tomorrow. And if you’ve ever held onto a grudge, you know it only deepens the hurt. Forgiveness, on the other hand, is the key that unlocks healing and brings people back together.
Now, let’s talk about gratitude. It goes hand in hand with forgiveness. Gratitude’s about noticing what’s good—even when things aren’t perfect. Sure, it’s easy to focus on what’s missing, or what went wrong. But if you make gratitude a habit, you start to realize there’s always something to appreciate—a warm smile, a shared meal, or just a moment of laughter.
I remember a family going through a rough patch financially. The days felt long, and worries seemed endless. But every night, they’d gather around their table and share one positive thing from their day. Did it erase their struggles? No. But it shifted their focus. Over time, they found strength in each other, and began to notice small blessings they might’ve missed before.
Forgiveness and gratitude aren’t just feel-good choices—they’re powerful tools for healing, both in relationships and in entire communities. When you choose to forgive, you break the cycle of hurt and retaliation. And when you express gratitude, you create an atmosphere where hope and positivity can grow.
This matters even more in families, where old wounds sometimes linger and daily stresses can make patience run thin. By choosing to forgive and be grateful, you help build a culture of understanding and real support. And here’s the thing—those choices ripple outward, shaping how you relate to friends, coworkers, even strangers.
So, here’s a gentle reminder to carry with you: forgiveness and gratitude aren’t one-time acts. They’re habits—skills you build, day by day. Sometimes they take patience, and sometimes, a willingness to see things differently. But if you stick with it, the rewards are huge. You’ll find more peace, stronger connections, and a deeper appreciation for the beauty woven into everyday life.

Chapter 5: Civility, Respect, and the Restoration of Decency. You know, these days, it can feel like every disagreement is just a hair away from turning into a full-blown argument. Differences? They're often met with suspicion or even anger. That’s why civility and respect—values that once seemed like a given—are more important now than ever. But here’s the thing: these aren’t just old-fashioned ideas. They’re essential if we want to build communities where everyone feels valued and truly heard. Picture this: a family gathering, maybe during the holidays. The conversation starts off easy, but suddenly, voices rise and tempers flare. For a moment, it feels like that argument might split the family in two. But then, someone takes a breath and really listens—like, not just waiting for their turn to speak, but actually hearing the other side. The whole mood shifts. By the end of the night, everyone still disagrees, but there’s a new sense of mutual respect. Civility, at its heart, is about more than just being polite. It’s the choice to treat others with dignity, even when you don’t see eye to eye. That means picking your words carefully, skipping the insults, and actually looking for common ground. Think about families—when civility is present, kids feel safe to speak up. And in our wider communities, civility lets people from all walks of life come together and work toward something bigger than themselves. And then there’s respect. It goes hand in hand with civility. Respect is about recognizing the worth in every person you meet. Sometimes, it’s as simple as holding the door for a stranger, listening without interrupting, or offering help with no strings attached. You don’t have to agree with someone to respect them. All it really takes is a little kindness and consideration. It’s easy to blame the loss of civility and respect on things like media, politics, or shifting social norms. But honestly, the real change starts closer to home. When parents show respect, their kids pick it up. When neighbors greet each other with a smile, the whole community feels more welcoming. I’m reminded of a workplace story where a project nearly fell apart because of clashing opinions. Instead of letting those differences turn into grudges, the team leader encouraged everyone to talk openly and listen to each other. With time, trust started to grow. And together, the team ended up achieving more than anyone expected. That experience really shows that civility and respect don’t make us weaker—they’re actually a source of real strength. Restoring decency, whether in our public lives or private ones, takes effort. It means resisting that knee-jerk reaction to snap back when someone’s rude. It’s about standing up for what matters, but doing it with humility and grace. And you’ll find, more often than not, when you choose civility and respect, others will follow your lead. So, just imagine a world where disagreements are handled with understanding. Where our differences aren’t something to fear, but something to celebrate. Where every person is treated with dignity. That’s the kind of society we can build, one choice at a time, simply by embracing civility and respect.

Chapter 6: Duty, Responsibility, and the Quiet Strength of Commitment.
There’s something really comforting about knowing there’s someone in your life who will always show up—no matter what. In a world where it feels like promises are broken left and right, and distractions are just part of daily life, that old-school sense of duty? It can seem almost heroic, can’t it?
But here’s the thing—it’s usually not about big, dramatic gestures. It’s the little, everyday actions that matter most. Think about a teenager, still half-asleep in the early morning, pulling themselves out of bed just to walk the family dog before school. Or the neighbor who, even with a calendar packed to the brim, always finds time to check in on an elderly friend each week.
These aren’t glamorous moments—they’re not Instagram-worthy. But they’re the real glue that keeps families, friendships, and communities together. Over time, you start to see that responsibility isn’t just about doing what you have to. It’s love, showing up in small but powerful ways.
And you know what else? When you get into the habit of keeping your word—even with the little things—you start to feel good about yourself. There’s a deep satisfaction in knowing people can count on you. For parents, it’s all about following through on promises, even when it would be so much easier not to. For kids, it might be as simple as finishing chores or homework, learning that what they do really does matter.
Of course, there are days when responsibility feels heavy. Imagine a single parent, totally wiped out after a long shift, still finding the energy to help with homework. Or a volunteer, tempted to skip out just this once, but remembering the faces of those who count on them. In those moments, the decision to show up—again and again—becomes a quiet act of courage.
One thing to remember: duty isn’t about being perfect. We all slip up, forget, or fall short sometimes. What really matters is being willing to try again, to say sorry when you need to, and to just keep moving forward. Little by little, those efforts build a foundation of trust and reliability.
Responsibility also means looking beyond yourself. It’s paying attention when someone else is struggling—and stepping in to help. It’s about caring for the places we all share, like tidying up after a community event or picking up litter at the park. These small actions, repeated over time, help everyone feel like they belong and that they’re part of something bigger.
So, as we wrap up this chapter, here’s the message to hold onto:
Commitment is a true form of love. When you honor your responsibilities, you’re helping to build families and communities that can make it through anything. The world might change, but the quiet strength of duty? That’s something that lasts.

Chapter 7: Faith, Hope, and the Light That Guides Us.
You know, there are times in life when the road ahead just isn’t clear. Maybe it’s illness, a loss, or a huge disappointment that leaves you feeling lost at sea. During these moments, faith and hope can become real lifelines—giving you strength to keep moving, even when you just don’t have all the answers.
Now, when we talk about faith here, it’s not just about religion. It’s that deep-down feeling that life has meaning, that good things are possible, and that you matter. For some, this faith comes from spiritual roots. For others, it’s found in the warmth of family, in the beauty of a sunrise, or just in the simple kindness of a stranger.
I’m reminded of a family facing a tough illness. The future feels shaky, and fear is everywhere. But every day, they sit together at the kitchen table—sharing stories, laughing, sometimes just sitting quietly. Their faith isn’t only in something bigger than themselves, but also in each other. And little by little, hope finds its way back in, giving them the courage to face whatever comes next.
Hope, really, is that quiet belief that tomorrow could be better than today. It’s what keeps you studying for that tough exam, or sending out another job application when you’re ready to give up. Hope doesn’t pretend everything’s perfect—it just refuses to let despair win.
And here’s something special: faith and hope get stronger when you’re surrounded by others. In tough times, people come together—maybe with a prayer, a home-cooked meal, or just by being there to listen. These simple acts remind us we’re not alone, that there’s always a reason to keep trying.
Of course, faith and hope aren’t always rock-solid. Doubts and tough days happen to everyone. But even then, just a tiny spark of hope can light the way forward. Sometimes, it’s a friend’s kind word, a sunrise after a long night, or just remembering a time you made it through something hard before.
So as we wrap up this chapter, here’s what really matters: take care of your faith and hope, whatever forms they take for you. They won’t erase pain, but they’ll help carry you through it. They give you the strength to keep going, to dream, and to build a brighter future—not only for yourself, but for everyone you care about.

Chapter 8: Self-Discipline and the Freedom of Restraint.
When you hear the word "freedom," what comes to mind? Maybe it’s the idea of doing whatever you want, whenever you want.
But if you’ve ever tried living that way, you probably found it doesn’t really lead to happiness or fulfillment. True freedom, as most of us discover, is actually found in self-discipline—the ability to make the right choice, even when it isn’t the easiest one.
Think about a child staring at a plate of cookies just before dinner. The urge to grab one is strong, but then a parent gently steps in, reminding them to wait. In that small moment, the child learns patience and the basics of self-control.
Or picture yourself late at night, scrolling through your phone when you know you should be sleeping. You decide to put the phone down and get some rest. These little decisions, repeated over and over, slowly shape who you are and build resilience.
Now, self-discipline isn’t about denying yourself joy or living without pleasure. It’s really about drawing healthy boundaries that protect what you value most—your health, your relationships, your goals.
For a student, it might mean switching off social media to focus on homework. For a couple, it could be making time for each other, even when the calendar’s packed and life feels overwhelming.
Of course, there are times when self-discipline feels tough—like when the alarm blares before sunrise and you’d rather sleep in, or when the fridge is packed with snacks and your willpower is wearing thin.
In those moments, it helps to remember what you’re working toward. The bigger picture—your dreams, your values—makes the effort worthwhile.
Throughout this chapter, you’ll find real stories of people who’ve practiced discipline until it became second nature. Take the athlete who trains day after day, even when motivation is nowhere to be found. Or the musician, repeating scales, knowing that mastery is built on repetition.
Over time, these habits open up new opportunities and bring a deeper sense of satisfaction.
But here’s something important: self-discipline isn’t about being perfect. It also means knowing when to rest, when to reach out for help, and yes, when to forgive yourself for slipping up.
It’s about making choices that reflect your deepest values, not chasing some impossible standard.
So, what’s the big takeaway? Self-discipline is a gift you give yourself. It gives you the freedom to chase your dreams, to nurture strong relationships, and to live with real integrity.
The world will always be full of temptations and distractions, but if you practice a little restraint, you’ll find a deeper, more lasting joy waiting for you.

Let’s dive into Chapter 9: Learning, Curiosity, and the Courage to Grow.
Think about this—every child starts out with a natural sense of wonder. They want to know how things work, why the sky is blue, or what makes a story end on a happy note. But as we get older, pressures and routines can chip away at that curiosity, sometimes replacing it with the fear of making mistakes. Still, the truth is, being eager to learn is one of the most powerful gifts we can nurture in ourselves and in those around us.
Picture a grandparent and child in the kitchen, working together to bake bread. The air is filled with questions—like, why does the dough rise, or what happens if you add too much salt? The grandparent might not know every answer, but they experiment together, learning as they go. In moments like these, it’s not just about baking; it’s about discovering new things and finding the courage to try, even if you don’t have it all figured out.
Here’s something to remember—real learning doesn’t just happen in classrooms or from textbooks. It happens in everyday conversations, in the mistakes we make, and in those quiet moments when we stop to think. Imagine a parent who’s puzzled by a new gadget, turning to their teenager for help. Suddenly the roles flip, and both come away with a deeper respect for what the other knows.
Curiosity is what sparks innovation and creativity. It’s what nudges us to pick up a new book, explore somewhere we’ve never been, or ask questions that others might not even think of. And the more you learn, the more you realize there’s still so much out there to discover.
Of course, being open to learning takes a bit of humility—it means admitting when you don’t know something, being brave enough to start as a beginner, and sometimes, having the guts to change your mind. It’s not always easy, but it’s the only way we truly grow.
The heart of this chapter is an invitation: let’s create spaces—at home, at work, or wherever we are—where questions are welcome and making mistakes is just a chance to learn. When kids see adults asking questions and learning new things, they’ll feel more comfortable doing the same. Over time, this builds a family or a community where curiosity and growth are just part of everyday life.
So, as we wrap up, here’s the key takeaway: keep that sense of curiosity alive. Try new things, chase down answers, and don’t be afraid to keep learning, no matter your age. The world is full of amazing things, just waiting for someone willing to ask, to listen, and to grow.

Chapter 10: Service, Generosity, and the Joy of Giving
You know, there’s a special kind of happiness that comes from helping others. It’s not like the quick thrill you get from a new gadget or a compliment—it runs deeper. It sticks with you. Service and generosity, as the book puts it, are those final, essential virtues that really complete the circle of a meaningful life.
Think back to a time when a community pulled together after a storm. Maybe you remember neighbors sharing tools, clearing away fallen branches, offering food to anyone who needed it. Nobody’s counting favors or waiting to be thanked. The whole focus is simply on helping. And in those moments, real generosity just... shines.
But service isn’t always about big heroic gestures. Sometimes, it’s as simple as listening when a friend needs to talk, volunteering for an hour at the local shelter, or sharing a meal with someone who’s feeling alone. Even the smallest acts can spark a ripple effect—lifting someone’s spirits, building connections, and reminding us all that we matter.
Generosity isn’t just about giving money or things. It’s about sharing your time, your attention, your kindness. Think about a busy parent who still finds a moment to help with homework, even with a mile-long to-do list. Or a stranger who offers a smile or a kind word in passing. Over time, these little habits add up, creating a culture where everyone feels supported—where abundance is shared, not hoarded.
Of course, service isn’t always easy. Some days, you’re running on empty, or the needs around you just feel too much. But here’s something to keep in mind—even small acts make a real difference. The goal isn’t to fix everything; it’s to do what you can, right where you are.
And here’s the beautiful part: the more you give, the richer your own life tends to become. Service gives you purpose, it deepens relationships, and it brings those moments of unexpected joy. It’s a reminder that everyone has something to offer, no matter what their circumstances.
So as we wrap up this final chapter, the message is simple, but powerful: a life filled with service and generosity is a life well-lived. When you give to others, you find meaning, connection, and a sense of belonging that lasts long after the moment has passed.

As we wrap up this journey through the often-overlooked virtues, let’s pause for a moment to remember what really matters. It’s not about chasing perfection, or holding on to some version of the past—it’s about rediscovering those simple, powerful habits that truly make life richer, deepen our relationships, and bring strength to our communities.
In a world that feels noisy and uncertain, the quiet work of building character—one choice at a time—still makes all the difference.
So, what should you take away from all this? First, it’s those small, everyday acts—showing kindness, keeping your word, reaching out to help—that shape families and communities over the years. Love, honesty, and forgiveness lay the foundation for trust and real healing.
When you practice responsibility and self-discipline, you create freedom and earn self-respect. And by staying curious and serving others, you keep your heart open and your life full of meaning.
Here’s the beautiful part: no matter where you start, or what you’re facing, you have the power to make a difference just by standing for something that matters.
If you ever feel overwhelmed by the pace of life, remember—you don’t have to change the world overnight. Start small. Maybe it’s a kind word, a promise kept, or a little extra patience. Let your home be the place where virtue is practiced, where mistakes are met with forgiveness, and where every effort is celebrated.
And when you stumble, as everyone does, just come back to the basics: love, honesty, gratitude, and service. It’s not always easy, but it’s always worth it. Every time you choose virtue over convenience, you’re planting a seed that will grow—sometimes quietly, sometimes in ways you don’t expect.
Over time, these choices heal hearts, strengthen homes, and inspire others to do the same. You’re not alone in this. By choosing to stand for something, you join a long tradition of people who believe that decency, kindness, and courage still matter.
And honestly, that’s how real change begins—one heart, one home, one day at a time.
